catalogue: Australian residential concrete foundations and reinforcement

ncc_references.relationship: Deemed-to-Satisfy pathway and limits for footings and slabs.
Physical footing, slab, reinforcement, fill and membrane terminology and construction provisions.

objects.name: concrete slab-on-ground assembly
objects.definition: A concrete floor and foundation assembly cast close to the ground and supported continuously or at its beams by prepared soil or fill.
functions: Form the ground floor
Transfer building and floor loads into the supporting ground
Provide a base for walls and floor finishes

cad.placement: At ground-floor level over prepared foundation material or fill
cad.opening: Contains designed penetrations, setdowns and recesses

notes: This is a generic assembly. Stiffened raft, waffle raft and footing slab are separate arrangements.

objects.name: stiffened raft slab
objects.definition: A slab-on-ground cast integrally with deeper edge and internal beams arranged as a stiff structural grid in excavated trenches.
functions: Support the building across the foundation area
Distribute loads through an integral slab-and-beam grid
Provide the ground floor surface

cad.pattern: Integral perimeter and internal beam grid
cad.placement: On prepared foundation material with beams extending into excavated trenches
cad.opening: Service penetrations and setdowns are coordinated through the slab

notes: Do not infer beam sizes or spacing without the applicable design pathway and project inputs.

objects.name: waffle raft slab
objects.definition: A raft slab cast over a regular field of void formers so reinforced concrete ribs form between the forms above a levelled base.
functions: Form the ground floor and foundation
Create a stiff rib grid with reduced concrete between ribs
Transfer building loads into the supporting ground

cad.pattern: Regular void-former grid with concrete ribs between units
cad.placement: Above a level prepared base
cad.opening: Pods and ribs must be coordinated around penetrations and setdowns

notes: The shorter term 'waffle slab' can also describe suspended ribbed slabs and is not accepted as an exact synonym.

objects.name: footing slab assembly
objects.definition: A ground-floor slab supported by separately poured strip footings or edge beams rather than an integral excavated raft-beam grid.
functions: Form the floor surface
Transfer floor and wall loads through the slab and separate footing system
Adapt the foundation arrangement to its site and wall construction

cad.pattern: Slab area bounded or supported by a separate footing layout
cad.placement: Over prepared fill and adjacent to or above separately formed footings
cad.opening: Contains coordinated penetrations and setdowns

notes: The RMIT training source is used for physical arrangement, not current site-class limits.

objects.name: strip footing system
objects.definition: A connected layout of continuous reinforced concrete footings running beneath loadbearing walls or other line loads.
functions: Support walls and line loads
Spread those loads into the foundation material
Tie the supported building footprint together where arranged as a grid

cad.pattern: Continuous runs beneath nominated walls, sometimes cross-connected as a grid
cad.placement: In excavated trenches on foundation material

objects.name: stump and pad footing system
objects.definition: A repeated foundation system in which vertical stumps support the floor structure and bear on individual pads or soleplates below.
functions: Support a suspended floor above ground
Transfer point loads through stumps to individual footings
Create a ventilated subfloor space where applicable

cad.pattern: Repeated point supports below bearer lines
cad.placement: Between individual pad footings and the suspended floor structure

objects.name: foundation material
objects.definition: The natural soil, rock or properly prepared material directly supporting a footing, slab beam, pad or pier.
functions: Receive loads from the footing system
Provide the bearing substrate beneath the building

cad.placement: Below and around footing excavations
cad.opening: Excavated to receive footings and services

notes: In engineering usage the foundation can mean the supporting ground; in everyday speech it often means the constructed footing system. The two senses must remain distinguishable.

objects.name: concrete slab panel
objects.definition: The relatively thin, broad concrete floor portion between or over the deeper beams of a residential slab foundation.
functions: Form the floor surface
Span or bear between supporting ribs, beams or ground
Distribute floor loads into the foundation system

cad.pattern: Planar regions bounded by beams, ribs, edges, joints or setdowns
cad.placement: At the top of the slab foundation
cad.opening: Contains service penetrations and may include lowered or recessed areas

objects.name: slab edge beam
objects.definition: A reinforced concrete beam running around the perimeter of a slab foundation and supporting its outer walls and edge.
functions: Support perimeter wall and slab-edge loads
Stiffen and define the slab perimeter
Transfer edge loads into the foundation material

cad.pattern: Continuous or joined runs around the slab perimeter
cad.placement: Along the external edge of a slab foundation
cad.opening: May be locally shaped at entries, recesses and service penetrations

objects.name: deepened edge beam
objects.definition: An edge beam made deeper than the adjoining slab panel so it reaches suitable support and provides greater stiffness or load capacity.
functions: Support the slab perimeter and external walls
Reach deeper foundation material or bridge local fill conditions
Increase perimeter stiffness

cad.pattern: Perimeter run with designed local or continuous depth
cad.placement: Along the slab edge extending below the slab panel

objects.name: slab internal beam
objects.definition: A deeper reinforced concrete strip formed within a slab foundation to stiffen the slab and support internal load lines.
functions: Stiffen the slab foundation
Support internal walls or concentrated load lines
Transfer loads through the slab to the ground

cad.pattern: Connected internal grid aligned to the design
cad.placement: Below the slab panel within the building footprint
cad.opening: Coordinated around penetrations and setdowns

objects.name: slab edge rebate
objects.definition: A continuous step or recess formed along a concrete slab edge to receive masonry veneer or cavity-wall construction and its drainage details.
functions: Provide a lowered bearing ledge for masonry
Create the geometry needed for wall flashing and drainage at the slab edge

cad.pattern: Continuous or segmented recess along nominated masonry wall edges
cad.placement: At the upper outer face of an edge beam
cad.opening: Is itself a subtractive concrete feature
cad.load: Bearing ledge geometry rather than a separate loadbearing member

notes: Stored as a drawable subtractive feature because the ontology permits openings; it is not a separate material component.

objects.name: strip footing
objects.definition: A continuous reinforced concrete footing running below a wall or another substantially continuous line load.
functions: Support a wall or line load
Spread that load into the foundation material
Connect with other footing runs where designed

cad.pattern: Continuous runs beneath walls with junctions and steps
cad.placement: In a footing trench on foundation material

notes: An edge beam may resemble a strip footing but is part of a slab edge; the roles remain separate.

objects.name: stepped strip footing
objects.definition: A strip footing divided into level runs joined by vertical or sloping transitions so it can follow a sloping site while maintaining suitable bearing.
functions: Carry a continuous wall load across changing ground levels
Maintain appropriate footing geometry on a slope

cad.pattern: Level footing runs connected at scheduled changes in level
cad.placement: In stepped excavations on a sloping site

objects.name: pad footing
objects.definition: An isolated concrete footing below a stump, pier, post or column that spreads a concentrated load into the foundation material.
functions: Support an individual vertical support
Spread a point load over a larger foundation area

cad.pattern: Repeated at point-support locations
cad.placement: Below a stump, pier, post or column on foundation material
cad.load: Isolated footing for a point load

notes: A timber soleplate can perform a similar load-spreading role under a timber stump but is a different physical object.

objects.name: subfloor stump
objects.definition: A short vertical support between an individual footing and a bearer or other suspended-floor member.
functions: Support bearers or floor beams above the ground
Transfer floor and wall loads down to a pad footing
Maintain the required subfloor level

cad.pattern: Repeated point supports below bearer lines
cad.placement: Vertically between pad footing and bearer
cad.load: Vertical compression support with possible lateral actions

objects.name: bulk pier
objects.definition: A local deep mass-concrete support below a slab edge beam or footing that carries load through fill or weak near-surface material to suitable natural ground.
functions: Provide deep local support below a slab or footing
Transfer load through unsuitable shallow material to stronger foundation material

cad.pattern: Discrete supports at designed positions
cad.placement: Below an edge beam or footing and extending through fill to natural soil
cad.end: Underside of slab beam or footing

notes: Exact distinction from bored piers and other deep foundations requires a dedicated foundation-systems pass.

objects.name: slab void former
objects.definition: A lightweight unit or form placed beneath a slab to reserve a void while concrete ribs and the slab panel are cast around or above it.
functions: Displace concrete from non-structural zones
Define the spacing and shape of concrete ribs
Remain in place or provide temporary form according to the system

cad.pattern: Repeated grid of units separated by rib spaces
cad.placement: On a level prepared base below the slab panel
cad.opening: Omitted or cut only according to the designed rib and penetration layout
cad.load: Forming unit, not assumed to be structural

notes: A waffle pod is a particular void-former type; not every void former is a waffle pod.

objects.name: waffle pod
objects.definition: A box-like lightweight void former used in a waffle raft slab to create regular reinforced concrete ribs between adjacent pods.
functions: Form the voids between waffle-slab ribs
Reduce concrete volume in the non-rib areas
Provide incidental thermal resistance where the product permits

cad.pattern: Repeated rectangular grid
cad.placement: On the prepared base between concrete rib lines
cad.opening: Pod pattern is coordinated around services and beam thickenings

objects.name: waffle raft rib
objects.definition: A narrow reinforced concrete beam cast in the gap between adjacent void formers beneath a waffle raft slab panel.
functions: Stiffen the waffle raft slab
Transfer slab and wall loads through the rib grid
Connect the slab panel with edge beams

cad.pattern: Orthogonal or designed grid between void formers
cad.placement: Below the slab panel between adjacent void former units
cad.opening: Rib layout controls where penetrations can pass

objects.name: structural concrete
objects.definition: A hardened composite material made from cementitious binder, water and aggregate, placed while workable to form slabs, beams, footings and other members.
functions: Form compression-resistant structural members
Encapsulate and work with reinforcement
Take the shape of the excavation or formwork during casting

cad.placement: Fills the designed member volume around reinforcement
cad.opening: Excluded from designed voids, rebates and penetrations
cad.load: Material used by concrete structural objects

notes: Concrete is the material; slab, beam and footing are construction roles made from it.

objects.name: under-slab damp-proofing membrane
objects.definition: A continuous flexible sheet placed beneath a slab-on-ground and its integral beams to limit moisture movement from the ground into the building.
functions: Limit ground moisture passing into the slab and building
Provide a continuous underlay around sealed penetrations and joints

cad.pattern: Continuous sheet field with lapped and sealed joints
cad.placement: Directly beneath the slab panel and extending beneath integral beams to its perimeter termination
cad.opening: Sealed around service penetrations

notes: The NCC uses both damp-proofing membrane and vapour barrier in this slab context; wider building-science usage may distinguish vapour-control functions.

objects.name: under-slab membrane joint tape
objects.definition: A compatible adhesive tape used to seal laps, repairs and local details in an under-slab damp-proofing membrane.
functions: Seal membrane sheet joints
Repair punctures with additional membrane material
Maintain continuity around detailed areas

cad.pattern: Continuous strips over membrane laps and repair edges
cad.placement: On the membrane surface at joints and repairs
cad.opening: Used as part of seals around penetrations

notes: The direction of the generated relationship records the associated membrane; the product must be compatible with the selected membrane system.

objects.name: under-slab membrane penetration sleeve
objects.definition: A close-fitting flexible sleeve or collar sealed to the under-slab membrane around a pipe or service passing through it.
functions: Maintain membrane continuity around a service penetration
Seal the gap between membrane and penetrating service

cad.pattern: One at each relevant service penetration
cad.placement: Around the service where it passes through the damp-proofing membrane
cad.opening: Surrounds the penetration

notes: Kept separate from termite, waterproofing and fire collars even when a proprietary product performs more than one role.

objects.name: concrete reinforcement assembly
objects.definition: The designed arrangement of steel bars, mesh, ligatures, ties and supports fixed in position before concrete is placed.
functions: Add tensile and crack-control capacity to concrete members
Keep individual reinforcement pieces in their designed relationship
Maintain reinforcement position during concreting

cad.pattern: Scheduled bars, strips, sheets and supports within concrete members
cad.placement: Inside the future concrete volume with designed cover
cad.opening: Reinforcement is detailed around openings and penetrations

objects.name: steel reinforcing bar
objects.definition: A straight, bent or coiled steel bar embedded in concrete to carry tensile forces, control cracking or reinforce a local detail.
functions: Reinforce concrete in a nominated direction
Carry tension and help control cracking
Provide local reinforcement at corners, beams, footings and other details

cad.pattern: Individual or repeated bars to a reinforcement schedule
cad.placement: Within slabs, beams, footings, pads and piers
cad.opening: Bent, trimmed or supplemented only to the design

objects.name: welded wire reinforcing fabric
objects.definition: A factory-welded grid of reinforcing wires or bars supplied as sheets or rolls for embedding in a concrete slab or other member.
functions: Reinforce a broad concrete area in two directions
Help control slab cracking
Provide repeatable bar spacing across a panel

cad.pattern: Tiled sheets or continuous rolls with scheduled laps
cad.placement: Within a slab panel or other broad concrete region
cad.opening: Cut and supplemented around penetrations only to the design

notes: Square mesh is a common form of welded wire fabric, not necessarily every possible fabric configuration.

objects.name: trench mesh
objects.definition: A long narrow prefabricated reinforcement strip with longitudinal bars joined by cross wires, sized for footings and slab beams.
functions: Provide continuous longitudinal reinforcement in footings and beams
Keep its main bars at a consistent spacing
Speed placement in narrow concrete members

cad.pattern: Continuous strips with scheduled laps along footings, ribs and beams
cad.placement: Within narrow footing and slab-beam volumes
cad.opening: Detailed around penetrations and junctions

objects.name: reinforcement ligature
objects.definition: A closed or partly closed bent reinforcing bar fitted around longitudinal bars to hold them in position and provide transverse restraint in a beam, column or pier cage.
functions: Hold longitudinal bars in their designed arrangement
Provide transverse reinforcement and restraint
Define the shape of a reinforcement cage

cad.pattern: Repeated transverse loops at scheduled spacing
cad.placement: Around longitudinal reinforcement bars
cad.opening: Shape follows the cage and designed penetrations

objects.name: reinforcement bar chair
objects.definition: A small wire, concrete or plastic support placed beneath or between reinforcement to hold it at the designed level while concrete is poured.
functions: Maintain concrete cover below reinforcement
Prevent reinforcement sagging or moving during concreting
Support mesh, bars or trench mesh at their scheduled elevation

cad.pattern: Repeated supports beneath mesh or bars at nominated spacing
cad.placement: Between reinforcement and the membrane, ground or formwork
cad.load: Temporary placement support remaining in concrete

objects.name: bar-chair base
objects.definition: A flat base fitted below a wire or narrow bar chair to spread its load on soft ground or a plastic membrane and reduce puncture risk.
functions: Stabilise a bar chair on a soft or flexible surface
Spread chair load
Reduce local damage to the under-slab membrane

cad.pattern: One beneath each applicable chair
cad.placement: Between the chair foot and soft ground or plastic membrane

notes: Preferred trade name needs additional public Australian manufacturer evidence.

objects.name: reinforcement tie wire
objects.definition: A small flexible wire twisted around intersecting reinforcement to hold bars and mesh in position before and during concrete placement.
functions: Temporarily secure reinforcement intersections
Keep bars, mesh and ligatures in their scheduled relationship during placement

cad.pattern: Discrete twists at scheduled reinforcement intersections
cad.placement: Around intersecting bars, mesh or ligatures
cad.load: Placement fastener, not primary structural reinforcement

notes: Existence is directly recognised by the NCC cover provision; detailed terminology needs another Australian source.

objects.name: slab edge insulation
objects.definition: A rigid or protected insulation strip installed against the vertical perimeter edge of a concrete slab to reduce heat flow through the slab edge.
functions: Reduce perimeter heat loss or heat gain
Improve the thermal continuity of the floor envelope

ncc_references.relationship: Thermal insulation associated with concrete slab-on-ground edges and heated or cooled slabs.

cad.pattern: Continuous vertical strip around applicable slab perimeter
cad.placement: Against the outside vertical face of the slab edge
cad.opening: Interrupted or detailed at entries and penetrations

notes: The insulation detail must preserve required termite inspection and moisture-management arrangements.

objects.name: concrete formwork
objects.definition: A temporary mould and support system that contains fresh concrete and gives a slab, beam, footing, wall or column its required shape until the concrete can support itself.
functions: Contain fresh concrete
Define member faces, edges, levels and rebates
Support wet concrete and construction loads until stripping

cad.pattern: Panels, boards and supports around the faces requiring containment
cad.placement: At exposed boundaries of fresh concrete
cad.opening: Forms box-outs, rebates and penetrations

notes: Temporary concrete works need a later dedicated pass covering shutters, walers, ties, props and braces.
